project.name: Claude-the-alligator
project.description: FRC robot code for SFUnity's 2026 competition robot, Claude (the alligator), built with WPILib and GradleRIO.

nodes.name: RobotContainer.java
nodes.summary: Central robot configuration class that instantiates all subsystems (drive, shooter, intake, climb, vision) with hardware or simulation IO implementations based on the current mode, wires up Xbox controller button bindings to commands, and configures fuel simulation for the 2026 game.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses WPILib Command-based paradigm with constructor switch on Constants.currentMode to select between REAL, SIM, and REPLAY hardware implementations.

nodes.name: RobotContainer
nodes.summary: Main robot container class that declares all subsystems, configures button-to-command mappings for an Xbox controller, provides autonomous command selection, and manages system alerts for CAN errors and low battery.

nodes.name: RobotContainer
nodes.summary: Constructor that instantiates all robot subsystems with appropriate IO implementations (real hardware, simulation, or replay stubs) based on the current robot mode, configures fuel simulation in SIM mode, and triggers button binding configuration.

nodes.name: configureButtonBindings
nodes.summary: Maps Xbox controller buttons and triggers to robot commands including joystick driving with speed limiting, intake toggling, shooting sequences, climbing, current zeroing, gyro reset, and controller rumble alerts tied to game shift timing.

nodes.name: checkAlerts
nodes.summary: Monitors controller connectivity, CAN bus error status, and battery voltage, setting appropriate WPILib alerts when thresholds are exceeded.

nodes.name: dashboardSetup
nodes.summary: Outputs dashboard color indicators based on game shift state: green when hub is active, white when inactive, blinking near shift end, and yellow during transitions.

nodes.name: TunerConstants.java
nodes.summary: Auto-generated CTRE Phoenix 6 swerve drive configuration defining PID gains, gear ratios, motor types, CAN IDs, encoder offsets, and physical dimensions for a four-module (FrontLeft, FrontRight, BackLeft, BackRight) Kraken X60 swerve drivetrain on a CANivore bus.
nodes.languageNotes: Generated by Tuner X Swerve Project Generator. Uses CTRE Phoenix 6 units library (Inches, Amps, Rotations, etc.) and SwerveModuleConstantsFactory builder pattern with heavy generics.

nodes.name: TunerConstants
nodes.summary: Static constants class holding all swerve drivetrain configuration including PID gains, gear ratios, module CAN IDs, encoder offsets, and module position coordinates for a four-module swerve drive system.

nodes.name: TunerSwerveDrivetrain
nodes.summary: Inner class extending CTRE SwerveDrivetrain with three constructor overloads for different configuration options (basic, with odometry frequency, and with standard deviations).

nodes.name: ClimbIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for the climbing mechanism, defining input logging fields (velocity, volts, current, position) and default methods for position setting and voltage control.

nodes.name: GyroIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for the gyroscope, defining input logging fields (connection status, yaw position/velocity, odometry timestamps) and default methods for updating inputs and setting yaw.

nodes.name: GyroIOPigeon2.java
nodes.summary: CTRE Pigeon 2 IMU implementation of GyroIO that reads yaw position and velocity via Phoenix 6 status signals and registers high-frequency odometry queues through PhoenixOdometryThread.

nodes.name: GyroIOPigeon2
nodes.summary: GyroIO implementation for CTRE Pigeon 2 IMU that configures the device using TunerConstants, sets up high-frequency yaw tracking via PhoenixOdometryThread, and converts raw signals to WPILib geometry types.

nodes.name: ModuleIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for a swerve drive module, defining input logging fields for drive and turn motors (position, velocity, volts, current, odometry data) and default methods for open-loop control, velocity control, position control, and PID tuning.

nodes.name: ModuleIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Physics simulation implementation of ModuleIO using WPILib DCMotorSim models for both drive and turn motors, with PID controllers for closed-loop velocity and position control and simulated odometry output at 50Hz.

nodes.name: ModuleIOSim
nodes.summary: Simulated swerve module using DCMotorSim with Kraken X60 motors, local PID gains separate from TunerConstants, and 20ms update loop producing synthetic drive/turn telemetry and odometry data.

nodes.name: ModuleIOTalonFX.java
nodes.summary: Real hardware implementation of ModuleIO for TalonFX-based swerve modules with CANcoder feedback, supporting both voltage and torque-current FOC control modes, configurable PID tuning, connection debouncing, and high-frequency odometry via PhoenixOdometryThread.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Java 17 switch expressions for selecting control request types based on module constants. Leverages CTRE Phoenix 6 status signals and the tryUntilOk retry utility for reliable hardware configuration.

nodes.name: ModuleIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: TalonFX swerve module IO implementation that configures drive and turn motors with gear ratios, current limits, and PID from TunerConstants/DriveConstants, reads status signals for telemetry, and registers high-frequency odometry queues.

nodes.name: PhoenixOdometryThread.java
nodes.summary: Singleton daemon thread for asynchronous high-frequency odometry sampling from Phoenix 6 devices, using CANivore waitForAll blocking on CAN FD or polling on CAN 2.0, with thread-safe signal registration and timestamp-corrected queue output.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ReentrantLock for thread safety and ArrayBlockingQueue for bounded inter-thread data passing. Implements singleton pattern with lazy initialization.

nodes.name: PhoenixOdometryThread
nodes.summary: Daemon thread singleton that registers Phoenix status signals and generic suppliers, samples them at the odometry frequency, computes latency-corrected FPGA timestamps, and publishes values to concurrent queues consumed by the Drive subsystem.

nodes.name: IntakePivotIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for the intake pivot mechanism, defining input logging fields (position, volts, current) and default methods for voltage control, position setting, and encoder resetting.

nodes.name: IntakeRollersIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for intake rollers, defining input logging fields (volts, current, velocity) and default methods for updating inputs, running at a voltage, and stopping.

nodes.name: IntakeRollersIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Minimal simulation implementation of IntakeRollersIO that tracks applied voltage state without physics modeling, providing basic stub behavior for simulation mode.

nodes.name: KickerIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for the kicker roller mechanism, defining input logging fields (volts, current, velocity, laser measurement) and default methods for voltage, duty cycle, and torque control modes.

nodes.name: SpindexerIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for the spindexer (spinning indexer) mechanism, defining input logging fields (velocity, position, volts, current) and a default voltage-based run method.

nodes.name: SpindexerIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Simple simulation implementation of SpindexerIO that models position change as proportional to applied voltage (1V = 0.1 rot/s at 20ms loop period), providing basic spindexer behavior for simulation mode.

nodes.name: FlywheelsIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for shooter flywheels, defining input logging fields (volts, velocity RPM, current) and default methods for stop, voltage, duty cycle, torque control, and velocity voltage control modes.

nodes.name: HoodIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for the shooter hood, defining input logging fields (position degrees, talon rotations, volts, current) and default methods for position control, voltage control, and encoder reset.

nodes.name: TurretIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for the shooter turret, defining input logging fields (dual encoder rotations, disconnection status, velocity, volts, current) and default methods for stopping, turning, and encoder reset.

nodes.name: VisionConstants.java
nodes.summary: Vision subsystem constants defining Limelight camera configurations (positions and orientations for four cameras: starboardFore/Aft, portFore/Aft), AprilTag field layout, ambiguity thresholds, raw detection field indices, and pipeline enumerations.

nodes.name: VisionConstants
nodes.summary: Constants class holding Limelight camera position/orientation configs, AprilTag field layout, MegaTag thresholds, raw detection index reference, and pipeline enum definitions for the vision subsystem.

nodes.name: VisionIOLimelight.java
nodes.summary: Limelight-based VisionIO implementation that uses MegaTag1 for the port-aft camera and MegaTag2 (with robot orientation injection) for all other cameras, extracting AprilTag pose estimates, tag IDs, and monitoring camera connectivity with latency-based disconnect alerts.

nodes.name: VisionIOLimelight
nodes.summary: VisionIO implementation for Limelight cameras that configures camera pose relative to robot center, reads AprilTag pose estimates via LimelightHelpers static methods, and monitors connectivity through timestamp-based latency detection.

nodes.name: LimelightHelpers.java
nodes.summary: Comprehensive third-party utility library (v1.14) providing static methods and data classes for interfacing with Limelight vision cameras via NetworkTables, including JSON result parsing, pose estimation (MegaTag1/MegaTag2), AprilTag/fiducial/barcode/classifier/detector result types, camera configuration, LED control, and snapshot management.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Jackson JSON annotations for deserialization of Limelight JSON output. All methods are static with NetworkTables entry caching via ConcurrentHashMap. Contains extensive inner classes for each detection target type.

nodes.name: LimelightHelpers
nodes.summary: Static utility class containing all Limelight camera interaction methods (NetworkTables reads/writes, JSON parsing, pose estimation, LED/pipeline control) and inner data classes for vision targets (Retro, Fiducial, Barcode, Classifier, Detector) and pose estimates.

nodes.name: Constants.java
nodes.summary: Defines global robot runtime constants including the operating mode (real, sim, replay), loop period, tuning mode flag, and the turret center transform used across subsystems.

nodes.name: Constants
nodes.summary: Final class holding global robot constants: operating mode enum (REAL/SIM/REPLAY), loop period, tuning flag, and turret center transform.

nodes.name: FieldConstants.java
nodes.summary: Comprehensive field geometry definitions including hub, bumps, trenches, tower, depot, and outpost positions, plus AprilTag layout loading with lazy initialization and double-checked locking.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Lombok annotations (@RequiredArgsConstructor, @Getter) for enum boilerplate reduction and volatile double-checked locking for thread-safe lazy initialization of AprilTag layouts.

nodes.name: FieldConstants
nodes.summary: Contains nested static classes (Hub, LeftBump, RightBump, LeftTrench, RightTrench, Tower, Depot, Outpost) defining all field element positions in meters from the blue alliance perspective, plus FieldType and AprilTagLayoutType enums for field layout management.

nodes.name: DriveCommands.java
nodes.summary: Factory class producing WPILib Command objects for various drive modes: joystick drive (field-relative), angle-locked drive, auto-aim toward the hub, snake drive, feedforward characterization, wheel radius characterization, and module tuning commands.

nodes.name: DriveCommands
nodes.summary: Static factory class with private constructor providing drive command builders including joystickDrive, joystickDriveAtAngle, autoAim, snakeDrive, feedforwardCharacterization, wheelRadiusCharacterization, and module tuning commands.

nodes.name: joystickDrive
nodes.summary: Creates a field-relative drive command controlled by joystick inputs with deadband, squared magnitude for precision, and alliance-aware rotation flipping.

nodes.name: joystickDriveAtAngle
nodes.summary: Creates a field-relative drive command using joystick for linear control and a profiled PID controller for angular control, enabling snapping to target angles.

nodes.name: autoAim
nodes.summary: Creates an auto-aiming drive command that rotates the robot to face the hub center using turret offset compensation, wrapping joystickDriveAtAngle.

nodes.name: feedforwardCharacterization
nodes.summary: Creates a sequential command to measure drive motor feedforward constants (kS, kV) by ramping voltage and performing linear regression on velocity/voltage samples.

nodes.name: wheelRadiusCharacterization
nodes.summary: Creates a parallel command to measure wheel radius by spinning the robot in place, comparing gyro rotation delta to wheel encoder deltas.

nodes.name: Drive.java
nodes.summary: Core swerve drivetrain subsystem managing four swerve modules, gyro integration, odometry updates, trajectory following with Choreo, SysId characterization, and module tuning. Coordinates with PoseManager for pose estimation.

nodes.name: Drive
nodes.summary: SubsystemBase implementation for the swerve drivetrain, handling module initialization, periodic odometry updates, velocity control, SysId routines, Choreo trajectory following, and module tuning.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Main periodic loop updating gyro inputs, module states, odometry measurements with timestamps, velocity data, gyro disconnect alerts, and vision-based gyro corrections.

nodes.name: followTrajectory
nodes.summary: Follows a Choreo trajectory sample using PID feedback on X, Y, and heading combined with feedforward velocities from the trajectory.

nodes.name: runVelocity
nodes.summary: Calculates and sends swerve module setpoints from desired chassis speeds using discretization for drift compensation.

nodes.name: DriveConstants.java
nodes.summary: Drive subsystem constants including max speed, track dimensions, swerve kinematics, bumper dimensions, and mode-dependent PID gains for drive and turn motors.

nodes.name: DriveConstants
nodes.summary: Constants class for drive subsystem with static initializer blocks that switch PID gains between real and sim modes, plus swerve kinematics, speed limits, and robot dimensions.

nodes.name: KickerIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Simulation implementation of the kicker roller hardware interface using a DCMotorSim to model a Kraken X60 motor with voltage clamping and periodic state updates.

nodes.name: KickerIOSim
nodes.summary: Implements KickerIO interface for physics simulation, modeling the kicker motor with DCMotorSim and providing voltage control, duty cycle, and torque control methods.

nodes.name: ShooterUtil.java
nodes.summary: Shooter calculation utility computing launching parameters (turret angle, hood angle, flywheel speed) using interpolating tree maps keyed by distance, with lookahead compensation for shoot-on-the-move (SOTM) via iterative time-of-flight convergence.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Java record type (LaunchingParameters) for immutable parameter bundles and InterpolatingDoubleTreeMap for piecewise-linear interpolation of empirically tuned shooting data.

nodes.name: ShooterUtil
nodes.summary: Manages distance-based interpolation maps for scoring and feeding in both real and sim modes, computing turret angle, hood angle, and flywheel speed from robot pose and target position with optional shoot-on-the-move lookahead.

nodes.name: getLaunchingParameters
nodes.summary: Computes launching parameters by calculating turret-to-target distance from the robot's predicted pose, then looking up hood angle and flywheel speed from the appropriate interpolation map based on scoring/feeding and real/sim mode.

nodes.name: getSOTMParameters
nodes.summary: Computes shoot-on-the-move parameters using iterative lookahead convergence (20 iterations) that accounts for turret velocity and time-of-flight to predict where the robot will be when the ball arrives at the target.

nodes.name: FlywheelsIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Simulation implementation of the flywheel hardware interface using a DCMotorSim to model a Kraken X60 motor with voltage clamping and RPM/current readback.

nodes.name: FlywheelsIOSim
nodes.summary: Implements FlywheelsIO interface for physics simulation, modeling the flywheel motor as a DCMotorSim with voltage control and state readback.

nodes.name: Vision.java
nodes.summary: Vision subsystem processing AprilTag detections from multiple cameras, filtering invalid measurements based on tag count, field boundaries, rotation speed, and distance, then feeding validated pose estimates to PoseManager with trust-scaled standard deviations.

nodes.name: Vision
nodes.summary: Extends VirtualSubsystem to process AprilTag vision data from multiple VisionIO cameras, applying multi-criteria rejection filters and trust scaling before submitting pose estimates to the SwerveDrivePoseEstimator.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Periodic vision processing loop iterating over cameras, validating AprilTag observations against multiple criteria (tag count, field bounds, rotation speed, distance), computing trust-weighted standard deviations, and submitting accepted measurements.

nodes.name: VisionIO.java
nodes.summary: Hardware abstraction interface for vision cameras defining AprilTag and object detection input structures with AutoLog annotation, plus default methods for input updates, naming, and thermal throttling.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AdvantageKit @AutoLog annotation to generate input logging boilerplate for AprilTagVisionIOInputs and ObjectDetectionVisionIOInputs.

nodes.name: AllianceFlipUtil.java
nodes.summary: Utility class flipping field coordinates (Translation2d, Rotation2d, Pose2d) based on the current driver station alliance color, mirroring both X and Y axes for red alliance.

nodes.name: AllianceFlipUtil
nodes.summary: Static utility class providing coordinate flipping methods that mirror field positions across both axes when the robot is on the red alliance.

nodes.name: GeomUtil.java
nodes.summary: Static geometry utility class providing conversion methods between WPILib types: Transform2d, Pose2d, Pose3d, Transform3d, Twist2d, and ChassisSpeeds, plus helper constructors for pure translations and rotations.

nodes.name: GeomUtil
nodes.summary: Static utility class with 13 conversion methods for WPILib geometry types, enabling concise kinematic chain construction and type interoperability.

nodes.name: PoseManager.java
nodes.summary: Central pose estimation manager wrapping SwerveDrivePoseEstimator, handling odometry updates, vision measurement fusion, velocity tracking, and game piece (fuel) position tracking with nearest-neighbor queries.

nodes.name: PoseManager
nodes.summary: Manages robot pose estimation combining swerve odometry and vision measurements, providing distance/angle calculations to targets, velocity data, and fuel (game piece) position tracking.

nodes.name: IntakePivotConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines tunable constants for the intake pivot subsystem including angle limits, gear ratio, jork voltage parameters, and position setpoints used for raising and lowering the intake arm.

nodes.name: IntakePivotIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Simulation implementation of the intake pivot IO interface using WPILib's SingleJointedArmSim for physics simulation, with a PID controller driving angle setpoints in a simulated environment.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the hardware IO interface pattern commonly used in AdvantageKit-based FRC projects to separate simulation from real hardware.

nodes.name: IntakePivotIOSim
nodes.summary: Simulated intake pivot IO using SingleJointedArmSim with PID-based position control, tunable PID gains, and voltage clamping.

nodes.name: IntakePivotVisualizer.java
nodes.summary: Provides 2D and 3D mechanism visualizations for the intake pivot, logging both Mechanism2d ligament angles and Pose3d outputs via AdvantageKit Logger for dashboard display.

nodes.name: IntakePivotVisualizer
nodes.summary: Creates and updates 2D mechanism and 3D pose visualizations for the intake pivot arm with tunable offset parameters for alignment.

nodes.name: IntakeRollersConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines constants for the intake rollers motor including CAN ID, inversion setting, position factor, and a tunable roller speed voltage.

nodes.name: IntakeRollersIOTalonFX.java
nodes.summary: TalonFX hardware implementation for intake rollers IO, configuring current limits and coast mode, providing voltage-based control for spinning the intake rollers.

nodes.name: IntakeRollersIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: Hardware IO class wrapping a TalonFX motor controller for the intake rollers, with voltage output control, current limits, and sensor input reading.

nodes.name: SpindexerConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines constants for the spindexer motor including CAN ID and tunable speed voltage setpoints for normal and slow operation modes.

nodes.name: SpindexerIOTalonFX.java
nodes.summary: TalonFX hardware implementation for the spindexer IO, configuring brake mode, current limits, clockwise-positive inversion, and providing voltage-based control with FOC enabled.

nodes.name: SpindexerIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: Hardware IO class wrapping a TalonFX motor for the spindexer, reading voltage, current, velocity, and position inputs while providing voltage-based run control.

nodes.name: ShooterConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines physical and tunable constants for the shooter subsystem including gravity, RPM limits, angle bounds, wheel radius, flywheel ratio, turret offset, trench avoidance parameters, and auto-mode shooting defaults.

nodes.name: ShooterVisualizer.java
nodes.summary: Provides 2D and 3D mechanism visualizations for both the turret and hood of the shooter, logging Mechanism2d and Pose3d outputs via AdvantageKit Logger with tunable offset parameters.

nodes.name: ShooterVisualizer
nodes.summary: Creates and updates 2D mechanism ligament visualizations and 3D pose transforms for the turret and hood, supporting tunable position offsets for dashboard alignment.

nodes.name: Flywheels.java
nodes.summary: WPILib SubsystemBase managing flywheel state machine (RUN, STOP, IDLE, VOLTS) with closed-loop velocity control, debounced at-goal detection, duty cycle spinup fallback, and command-based stop functionality.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a state machine pattern with enum-based states and periodic dispatch. Substantial commented-out code suggests iterative tuning of flywheel control strategies.

nodes.name: Flywheels
nodes.summary: Flywheel subsystem class extending SubsystemBase, managing a state machine for flywheel control with velocity setpoints, at-goal debouncing, and multiple control modes including duty cycle and velocity voltage.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Periodic loop that processes IO inputs, logs subsystem state, updates debouncer parameters, and dispatches to the appropriate flywheel control mode based on current state.

nodes.name: runVelocity
nodes.summary: Runs closed-loop velocity control on the flywheels, switching between duty cycle and velocity voltage modes based on RPM error threshold, with debounced at-goal detection.

nodes.name: FlywheelsConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines constants for the flywheel motors including CAN IDs for leader/follower, gear ratio, and tunable tolerances and debounce times for torque current control and at-goal detection.

nodes.name: FlywheelsIOTalonFX.java
nodes.summary: TalonFX hardware implementation for dual-motor flywheel IO using a leader/follower configuration with opposed alignment, providing duty cycle, velocity voltage, torque current FOC, and voltage control modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Phoenix 6 leader/follower motor pattern with MotorAlignmentValue.Opposed for counter-rotating flywheels, with multiple control request objects pre-allocated for performance.

nodes.name: FlywheelsIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: Dual-motor TalonFX flywheel IO with leader/follower configuration, configuring PID gains, current limits, gear ratio feedback, and providing multiple control mode methods including velocity voltage and torque current FOC.

nodes.name: LoggedTunableNumber.java
nodes.summary: Utility class providing runtime-tunable numbers via NetworkTables dashboard in tuning mode, with change detection and callback support for efficient parameter hot-swapping during development.
nodes.languageNotes: Originally from FRC 6328 (Mechanical Advantage). Uses a per-caller HashMap keyed by hashCode for independent change tracking across multiple consumers of the same tunable number.

nodes.name: LoggedTunableNumber
nodes.summary: Tunable number class that reads from NetworkTables in tuning mode or returns a default value, with per-caller change detection via hasChanged() and static ifChanged() callback utilities.

nodes.name: ifChanged
nodes.summary: Static method that checks if any of the provided tunable numbers have changed for the given caller ID and runs the callback with the current values array if so.

nodes.name: Autos.java
nodes.summary: Defines all autonomous routines for the robot using Choreo trajectory following, including multi-segment scoring, feeding, climbing, and bump autos. Orchestrates subsystem commands via RobotCommands helpers and exposes the selected auto via LoggedAutoChooser.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Choreo AutoFactory/AutoRoutine API with time-based event triggers (atTime) to sequence subsystem commands along pre-planned trajectories.

nodes.name: Autos
nodes.summary: Constructor that initializes the Choreo AutoFactory, registers all available autonomous routines with the chooser, and optionally adds SysId/tuning routines when not connected to FMS.

nodes.name: ScoreCenterClimbAutoRoutine
nodes.summary: Autonomous routine that drives to center, intakes a game piece, scores it, then climbs.

nodes.name: ScoreUpperCenterClimbAutoRoutine
nodes.summary: Autonomous routine that drives through the upper center path, intakes, scores, and climbs.

nodes.name: FeedAutoRoutine
nodes.summary: Autonomous routine that drives a feed path while simultaneously intaking and shooting game pieces.

nodes.name: LowerFeedAutoRoutine
nodes.summary: Autonomous routine that runs the lower feed trajectory while intaking and shooting game pieces.

nodes.name: DoubleScoreUpperLoop
nodes.summary: Two-segment autonomous routine that scores twice via the upper loop path, using jork feeding and unjam sequences between scores.

nodes.name: DoubleScoreLowerLoop
nodes.summary: Two-segment autonomous routine that scores twice via the lower loop path, using jork feeding and unjam sequences between scores.

nodes.name: DoubleLowerBump
nodes.summary: Two-segment autonomous routine that bumps and scores twice through the lower path with timed transitions.

nodes.name: DoubleUpperBump
nodes.summary: Two-segment autonomous routine that bumps and scores twice through the upper path with timed transitions.

nodes.name: CompleteLowerFeed
nodes.summary: Autonomous routine that runs a complete lower feed path with intake, shoot, stop-shoot, and jork phases.

nodes.name: CompleteUpperFeed
nodes.summary: Autonomous routine that runs a complete upper feed path with intake, shoot, stop-shoot, and jork phases.

nodes.name: RobotCommands.java
nodes.summary: Static command factory class providing reusable composite commands for common robot actions: shooting, intaking, stowing, jorking (oscillating intake pivot), unjamming, and system tests. Used extensively by Autos and RobotContainer.

nodes.name: readyThenShoot
nodes.summary: Spins up kicker and shooter, waits until ready, then runs the spindexer to feed game pieces while avoiding shooting behind the hub.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Sequentially tests the turret, hood, intake pivot, spindexer, kicker, intake rollers, and flywheels to verify all subsystems function correctly.

nodes.name: Climb.java
nodes.summary: Subsystem controlling the climbing mechanism with voltage-based up/down commands and position-feedback-based volt commands for extending and retracting the climber.

nodes.name: Climb
nodes.summary: WPILib SubsystemBase for the climb mechanism, providing commands for climbing up, climbing down, idle, and voltage-controlled extend/retract with position limits.

nodes.name: IntakePivot.java
nodes.summary: Subsystem controlling the intake pivot arm with position-based raise/lower commands, current-based zeroing, and a 'jork' oscillation mode that rapidly raises and lowers the intake to settle game pieces.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses stator current debouncing for zero-position detection and WPILib Mechanism2d visualization via IntakePivotVisualizer.

nodes.name: IntakePivot
nodes.summary: WPILib SubsystemBase for the intake pivot arm providing raise, lower, jork, stator jork, and current zeroing commands with visualizer integration.

nodes.name: IntakeRollers.java
nodes.summary: Simple subsystem controlling the intake roller motors with commands for intaking, stopping, and ejecting game pieces at configurable voltage.

nodes.name: Kicker.java
nodes.summary: Subsystem for the kicker roller that feeds game pieces to the shooter using velocity control with duty-cycle and torque-current FOC modes, LaserCAN-based launch counting, and a state machine for run/stop/backwards control.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a hybrid velocity control strategy: duty cycle for spinup, then switches to torque-current FOC once near setpoint, using debounced tolerance checks.

nodes.name: Kicker
nodes.summary: WPILib SubsystemBase for the kicker with state machine control (RUN/STOP/BACKWARDS), velocity-based feeding, LaserCAN fuel counting, and debounced torque-current switching.

nodes.name: KickerConstants.java
nodes.summary: Constants for the kicker subsystem including motor ID, LaserCAN ID, RPM setpoint, torque control tolerances, and debounce timing, all using LoggedTunableNumber for runtime adjustment.

nodes.name: KickerIOTalonFX.java
nodes.summary: Hardware implementation of the KickerIO interface using a TalonFX motor controller and GrappleRobotics LaserCAN sensor, providing voltage, duty-cycle, and velocity torque-current FOC control modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CTRE Phoenix 6 VelocityTorqueCurrentFOC and DutyCycleOut control requests, plus GrappleRobotics LaserCAN for distance-based game piece detection.

nodes.name: KickerIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: KickerIO implementation that configures a TalonFX with current limits, coast mode, and torque control parameters, reads LaserCAN measurements for fuel detection, and provides multiple motor control modes.

nodes.name: Spindexer.java
nodes.summary: Subsystem controlling the spindexer (spinning indexer) roller that feeds game pieces into the shooter, with stator-current-based jam detection and LED feedback for jam status.

nodes.name: Spindexer
nodes.summary: WPILib SubsystemBase for the spindexer providing run, run-until-jammed, run-back, run-back-until-jam, and stop commands with debounced stator current jam detection.

nodes.name: Hood.java
nodes.summary: Subsystem controlling the shooter hood angle with position-based control, current-based zeroing, and simulation-aware angle reporting for shot trajectory adjustment.

nodes.name: Hood
nodes.summary: WPILib SubsystemBase for the shooter hood providing angle setting, at-goal checking, current-based zero calibration, and simulation-aware angle reading.

nodes.name: GeneralUtil.java
nodes.summary: Abstract utility class providing a tolerance-based equality check and a subsystem command-logging helper used across all subsystems for AdvantageKit telemetry.

nodes.name: LoggedAutoChooser.java
nodes.summary: AdvantageKit-compatible auto routine chooser that lazily loads autonomous routines on selection via NetworkTables, providing dashboard integration for runtime autonomous mode selection with replay support.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends LoggedNetworkInput from AdvantageKit for deterministic replay support. Uses lazy loading (Supplier<AutoRoutine>) to defer trajectory parsing until the routine is actually selected.

nodes.name: LoggedAutoChooser
nodes.summary: Choreo-integrated SendableChooser replacement that lazily loads AutoRoutines, updates selection only when disabled, and provides AdvantageKit logging/replay support via LoggedNetworkInput.

nodes.name: ClimbConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines physical constants and tunable PID parameters for the climb subsystem elevator, including motor ID, gear ratio, mass, drum radius, height limits, and mode-specific PID gains (real vs simulation).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a static initializer block with a switch on Constants.currentMode to select between real and simulation PID gains at class load time.

nodes.name: ClimbIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Simulation implementation of the ClimbIO interface using WPILib's ElevatorSim physics model with a PID controller, allowing the climb subsystem to be tested without real hardware.

nodes.name: ClimbIOTalonFX.java
nodes.summary: Hardware implementation of the ClimbIO interface using a CTRE TalonFX motor controller with position voltage control, current limiting, and brake mode for the climb elevator mechanism.

nodes.name: IntakePivotIOTalon.java
nodes.summary: Hardware implementation of IntakePivotIO using a TalonFX motor with Motion Magic profiled positioning, arm cosine gravity compensation, and encoder reset capability for the intake pivot mechanism.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CTRE Motion Magic for smooth profiled motion with configurable acceleration and cruise velocity, combined with cosine gravity feedforward for arm-type mechanisms.

nodes.name: HoodConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines physical constants for the shooter hood mechanism including motor ID, gear ratio, angular position limits in degrees and radians, angle tolerance, and arm length.

nodes.name: HoodIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Simplified simulation implementation of HoodIO that directly sets the hood angle without physics simulation, using a SingleJointedArmSim that is initialized but not actively stepped.

nodes.name: HoodIOTalonFX.java
nodes.summary: Hardware implementation of HoodIO using a TalonFX motor with position voltage control, gain scheduling, gravity feedforward, and Motion Magic configuration for precise hood angle positioning with position clamping and offset correction.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CTRE gain scheduling with discontinuous kP behavior and closed-loop error thresholds for fine-tuned position control around the setpoint.

nodes.name: PhoenixUtil.java
nodes.summary: Utility class providing a retry helper for CTRE Phoenix 6 motor controller configuration commands, attempting a command up to a specified number of times and raising a WPILib Alert on persistent failure.

nodes.name: tryUntilOk
nodes.summary: Retries a Phoenix 6 StatusCode-returning command up to maxAttempts times, returning on success or posting an error Alert if all attempts fail.

nodes.name: ClimbIOSim
nodes.summary: Simulation implementation of ClimbIO using WPILib ElevatorSim physics with PID position control and direct voltage output.

nodes.name: ClimbIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: Hardware ClimbIO implementation using a TalonFX motor controller with position voltage and voltage-out control modes, current limiting, and brake mode.

nodes.name: IntakePivotIOTalon
nodes.summary: Hardware IntakePivotIO implementation using a TalonFX motor with Motion Magic profiled positioning, arm cosine gravity compensation, and encoder management.

nodes.name: HoodIOSim
nodes.summary: Simplified HoodIO simulation that directly tracks the set angle without stepping the physics sim, providing basic angle feedback for testing.

nodes.name: HoodIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: Hardware HoodIO implementation using TalonFX with gain-scheduled position control, gravity feedforward, Motion Magic, and position offset correction for precise hood angle control.

nodes.name: Robot.java
nodes.summary: Main robot entry point extending LoggedRobot that initializes AdvantageKit logging, instantiates RobotContainer, and dispatches mode-specific lifecycle callbacks (autonomous, teleop, test, simulation).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Java 17+ switch expressions for metadata recording and mode-based data receiver setup.

nodes.name: Robot
nodes.summary: Top-level robot class that configures AdvantageKit logging per mode (REAL, SIM, REPLAY), creates the RobotContainer, and delegates periodic work to VirtualSubsystem and CommandScheduler.

nodes.name: robotPeriodic
nodes.summary: Called every loop cycle to run VirtualSubsystem periodic updates, the CommandScheduler, and RobotContainer dashboard/alert checks.

nodes.name: autonomousInit
nodes.summary: Retrieves and schedules the autonomous command selected via RobotContainer at the start of autonomous mode.

nodes.name: Leds.java
nodes.summary: Singleton LED subsystem extending VirtualSubsystem that manages a 150-LED addressable strip, displaying team colors, alliance-aware patterns, e-stop breathing, and scoring/jamming indicators.

nodes.name: Leds
nodes.summary: Singleton VirtualSubsystem managing addressable LEDs with patterns for disabled, autonomous, e-stop, jamming, and shooting states via WPILib LEDPattern API.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Updates LED pattern each cycle based on robot state: e-stop, disabled alliance colors, autonomous gradient, or enabled shooting/jamming indicators, then writes to the LED buffer.

nodes.name: Shooter.java
nodes.summary: High-level shooter coordinator subsystem that orchestrates turret aiming, hood angle, and flywheel speed based on pose estimation, with support for scoring vs feeding modes, trench avoidance, and fuel simulation integration.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavily uses WPILib Command-based patterns with inline lambda commands and LoggedTunableNumber for runtime tuning via NetworkTables.

nodes.name: Shooter
nodes.summary: VirtualSubsystem coordinating Flywheels, Turret, and Hood subsystems to aim and shoot fuel, with auto feed-vs-score logic, trench avoidance, and simulation fuel launching.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Main periodic loop that computes turret angle from pose-to-target geometry, sets hood and flywheel via ShooterUtil, handles feed vs score mode switching, hood safety, and launches fuel in simulation.

nodes.name: TrenchAvoidence
nodes.summary: Trench avoidance logic that monitors robot position and velocity relative to trench boundaries and drops the hood when approaching a trench to avoid collisions.

nodes.name: FuelSim.java
nodes.summary: Comprehensive 3D physics simulation for fuel (game pieces) on the FRC field, handling gravity, air resistance, field/wall/trench/hub collisions, robot bumper interactions, intake detection, and hub scoring with spatial-hash grid optimization.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses spatial hashing (grid cells) for O(n) fuel-fuel collision detection instead of naive O(n^2), and models physical constants like drag coefficient and coefficient of restitution for realistic ball physics.

nodes.name: FuelSim
nodes.summary: Physics engine simulating fuel (ball) dynamics on the FRC field including projectile motion, collisions with field geometry, hubs, trenches, robots, and intakes, with NetworkTables logging.

nodes.name: Fuel
nodes.summary: Inner class representing a single fuel game piece with position, velocity, physics update step (gravity + drag), and collision handling against field surfaces, walls, hubs, and trenches.

nodes.name: Hub
nodes.summary: Static inner class modeling blue and red hubs with scoring detection (fuel passing through entry zone), collision responses for hub sides and nets, and score tracking.

nodes.name: stepSim
nodes.summary: Advances the physics simulation by one timestep, running subtick iterations of fuel updates, fuel-fuel collisions, robot collisions, and intake checks, then logs positions.

nodes.name: launchFuel
nodes.summary: Spawns a fuel at the turret pose with computed launch velocity from hood angle and turret yaw, adding robot field velocity for shoot-on-the-move simulation.

nodes.name: handleRobotCollision
nodes.summary: Resolves collision between a fuel and the robot's rectangular bumper footprint by finding the minimum penetration axis and applying impulse with a coefficient of restitution.

nodes.name: handleFuelCollisions
nodes.summary: Uses a spatial hash grid to efficiently detect and resolve pairwise fuel-fuel collisions, checking only neighboring cells for O(n) average performance.

nodes.name: spawnStartingFuel
nodes.summary: Populates the field with starting fuel positions in the neutral zone center grid and alliance depot areas matching the game's initial fuel layout.

nodes.name: ShiftHelpers.java
nodes.summary: Utility class for tracking match shift timing and hub activity in the 2026 FRC game, providing methods to determine current/next shift, time remaining, and whether a hub is active for a given alliance based on auto winner.
nodes.languageNotes: Models the 2026 FRC game's shift-based hub activation system where auto winner/loser alternate hub access across seven timed shifts.

nodes.name: ShiftHelpers
nodes.summary: Static utility providing shift timing queries (getCurrentShift, getNextShift, isActive) and match time calculation for the 2026 game's alternating hub activation system.

nodes.name: getCurrentShift
nodes.summary: Returns the current match Shift based on elapsed match time, iterating through shift end times to find the active period.

nodes.name: getMatchTime
nodes.summary: Converts DriverStation countdown timer to an ascending match time (0-160 seconds), handling autonomous and teleop phases separately.

nodes.name: getAutoWinner
nodes.summary: Parses the FMS game-specific message to determine which alliance won the autonomous period, returning the winning Alliance or empty.

nodes.name: VirtualSubsystem.java
nodes.summary: Abstract base class that auto-registers subclasses in a static list, enabling periodicAll() to invoke every VirtualSubsystem's periodic() method from the main robot loop without requiring WPILib Subsystem registration.
nodes.languageNotes: Self-registering pattern via constructor that adds 'this' to a static list, providing a lightweight alternative to WPILib's built-in Subsystem lifecycle.

nodes.name: VirtualSubsystem
nodes.summary: Abstract class with static self-registration: each subclass instance auto-adds to a static list, and periodicAll() iterates them for periodic updates outside the WPILib command scheduler.

nodes.name: Turret.java
nodes.summary: WPILib subsystem controlling the shooter turret with dual-encoder absolute position solving, trapezoid motion profiling, safety e-stop logic, and multi-revolution angle wrapping to keep the turret within legal bounds.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends WPILib SubsystemBase and uses AdvantageKit's AutoLogOutput annotation for automatic telemetry logging. Implements a dual-encoder disambiguation algorithm to determine absolute turret position from two encoders with coprime gear ratios.

nodes.name: Turret
nodes.summary: Main turret subsystem class that manages position control, encoder health monitoring with debouncers, emergency-disable safety checks, and multi-revolution angle selection for shortest-path turret rotation.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Periodic update loop that reads encoder inputs, resolves absolute position via dual-encoder algorithm, enforces safety bounds with debounced out-of-bounds and encoder-broken detection, selects the optimal multi-revolution angle, and commands the turret motor.

nodes.name: getMotorOffsetDegsTestable
nodes.summary: Testable dual-encoder disambiguation algorithm that iterates candidate turret positions based on encoder1's possible rotations and validates against encoder2's expected reading to determine the absolute turret angle in degrees.

nodes.name: getMotorOffsetDegs
nodes.summary: Reads both encoder positions, normalizes them to [0,1) range, and delegates to getMotorOffsetDegsTestable for absolute position computation.

nodes.name: TurretConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines all turret mechanical constants including CAN IDs, gear ratios for turret/encoder1/encoder2, angular limits with buffer zones, tolerance thresholds, and tunable parameters for the turret subsystem.

nodes.name: TurretConstants
nodes.summary: Constants class holding turret hardware IDs, gear ratios (turret=85, encoder1=11, encoder2=10), angle limits (0-372 degrees), buffer zones, tolerances, and a tunable away-from-setpoint threshold.

nodes.name: TurretIOSim.java
nodes.summary: Simulation implementation of the TurretIO interface using WPILib's DCMotorSim with a Kraken X60 FOC motor model, providing physics-based turret behavior for testing without hardware.

nodes.name: TurretIOSim
nodes.summary: Simulated turret IO using DCMotorSim with a Kraken X60 FOC gearbox, implementing proportional voltage control for turnTurret and providing simulated encoder/velocity readings in updateInputs.

nodes.name: TurretIOTalonFX.java
nodes.summary: Hardware implementation of TurretIO using a CTRE TalonFX motor controller with MotionMagic position control, two CANcoder absolute encoders, FOC enabled, current limiting, and brake-mode configuration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CTRE Phoenix 6 API with MotionMagicVoltage control mode for smooth trapezoidal motion profiling on the motor controller itself, offloading trajectory computation from the RoboRIO.

nodes.name: TurretIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: Real-hardware turret IO implementation with TalonFX motor, two CANcoders for absolute positioning, MotionMagic control with PID gains (kP=2, kV=0.1), 80A stator / 60A supply current limits, and encoder disconnect detection.

nodes.name: TurretIOTalonFX
nodes.summary: Constructor that initializes the TalonFX and both CANcoders, configures motor inversion, brake mode, current limits, PID slot 0 gains, and MotionMagic velocity/acceleration parameters, then applies configuration with retry logic.

nodes.name: updateInputs
nodes.summary: Reads all sensor data from the TalonFX motor and both CANcoders, populating the IO inputs struct with voltage, velocity, current, position, and encoder connectivity status.

nodes.name: encoderReading.java
nodes.summary: JUnit 5 test class that validates the turret's dual-encoder position disambiguation algorithm by instantiating a Turret with TurretIOSim and calling getMotorOffsetDegsTestable with known encoder values.

nodes.name: encoderReading
nodes.summary: JUnit 5 test fixture that creates a Turret with a simulated IO layer and tests the getMotorOffsetDegsTestable method with specific encoder readings to verify position disambiguation logic.

nodes.languageNotes: Choreo .chor files are JSON-based project files that define robot physical parameters (mass, wheelbase, gearing) and reusable pose variables for trajectory planning.

nodes.name: Main.java
nodes.summary: Application entry point that bootstraps the FRC robot by calling RobotBase.startRobot with the Robot class constructor reference. Contains no other logic per WPILib convention.

nodes.name: Module.java
nodes.summary: Represents a single swerve drive module, encapsulating drive/turn motor IO, odometry position tracking, setpoint optimization with cosine scaling, and hardware disconnect alert management.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Java generics with CTRE Phoenix 6 SwerveModuleConstants parameterized by TalonFX and CANcoder configuration types. Implements the AdvantageKit IO pattern for hardware abstraction.

nodes.name: Module
nodes.summary: Swerve module class managing a single drive/turn motor pair with odometry integration, setpoint optimization, characterization support, and hardware disconnect alerts via AdvantageKit logging.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Updates module inputs from hardware IO, calculates odometry positions from drive encoder radians and turn angles, and refreshes hardware disconnect alerts.

nodes.name: runSetpoint
nodes.summary: Runs the swerve module to a target state by optimizing the velocity setpoint direction, applying cosine scaling, and commanding drive velocity and turn position.

nodes.name: ShooterUtilOld.java
nodes.summary: Legacy shooter utility implementing projectile motion calculations to determine optimal launch angle, RPM, and turn compensation for scoring, with fallback logic when max RPM is exceeded.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses classical projectile motion equations with quadratic solving for angle correction when the required velocity exceeds the shooter's maximum RPM of 3500.

nodes.name: ShooterUtilOld
nodes.summary: Static utility class containing projectile motion calculations for the shooter subsystem, including optimal shot computation, time-of-flight estimation, and turn angle compensation for lateral movement.

nodes.name: calculateOptimalShot
nodes.summary: Calculates optimal shooter angle and RPM for a given target distance using projectile motion physics, falling back to quadratic angle correction when required velocity exceeds the 3500 RPM cap.

nodes.name: calculateTimeOfFlight
nodes.summary: Estimates the time of flight for a projectile given horizontal distance, launch angle, and shooter RPM by computing exit velocity and dividing distance by horizontal velocity component.

nodes.name: AlwaysLoggedTunableNumber.java
nodes.summary: Provides a dashboard-tunable number that is always logged via NetworkTables regardless of tuning mode, with change detection support for efficient parameter updates during runtime.

nodes.name: AlwaysLoggedTunableNumber
nodes.summary: Wraps a LoggedNetworkNumber to provide always-on dashboard tuning with per-caller change detection via hash-based tracking, and static convenience methods for batch change callbacks.

nodes.name: WPILOGWriter9038.java
nodes.summary: Custom AdvantageKit log data receiver that writes robot telemetry to WPILOG files with automatic filename generation based on timestamps and match info, AdvantageScope integration for replay, and support for all WPILib loggable types.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the LogDataReceiver interface from AdvantageKit (org.littletonrobotics.junction). Uses Java switch expressions for AdvantageScopeOpenBehavior enum and traditional switch statements for type-based data appending across 11 loggable types.

nodes.name: WPILOGWriter9038
nodes.summary: LogDataReceiver implementation that manages WPILOG file lifecycle including creation, auto-renaming based on match data, incremental field encoding with change detection, and optional AdvantageScope log file handoff.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Initializes the WPILOG file by creating the log directory, opening a DataLogWriter with AdvantageKit headers, and resetting entry ID tracking maps.

nodes.name: end
nodes.summary: Closes the WPILOG file and optionally writes the log path to a temp file for AdvantageScope to automatically open during simulation replay.

nodes.name: putTable
nodes.summary: Core logging method that processes a LogTable by auto-renaming the file based on match info, encoding changed fields across all 11 loggable types, and flushing to disk each cycle.

nodes.name: IntakeRollersIOSim
nodes.summary: Simulation implementation of IntakeRollersIO that tracks applied voltage and current without real hardware.

nodes.name: SpindexerIOSim
nodes.summary: Simulation implementation of SpindexerIO that simulates position changes based on applied voltage.

nodes.name: toggleLimitSpeed
nodes.summary: Toggles between limited and unlimited drive speed based on a boolean supplier, delegating to joystickDriveLimitSpeed or joystickDrive accordingly.

nodes.name: intake
nodes.summary: Creates a command that runs intake rollers and lowers the intake pivot simultaneously.

nodes.name: stopShoot
nodes.summary: Creates a command that stops the spindexer, waits briefly, then disables shooting and stops the kicker.

nodes.name: jork
nodes.summary: Creates a command that stops intake rollers and runs the intake pivot jork motion.

nodes.name: unjam
nodes.summary: Creates a command that runs the spindexer backwards until jammed while running the kicker and test flywheel RPM.

nodes.name: logSubsystem
nodes.summary: Logs the current command name of a subsystem to AdvantageKit's Logger under the CurrentCmds key.

nodes.name: getNextShift
nodes.summary: Returns an Optional containing the next game Shift based on match time, or empty if disabled or between auto and teleop.

nodes.name: SimpleShoot
nodes.summary: Creates the Simple Shoot auto routine that follows the SimpleShoot trajectory and then shoots.

nodes.name: CenterShoot
nodes.summary: Creates the Center Shoot auto routine that follows the CenterShoot trajectory and then shoots.

layers.name: Robot Core
layers.description: Main entry points, lifecycle management, and central dependency injection hub (Robot, RobotContainer, Main) that bootstraps all subsystems and wires controller bindings via the WPILib command-based framework.

layers.name: Commands & Autonomous
layers.description: Command factories and autonomous routine definitions that compose subsystem actions into drive modes, shooting sequences, intaking workflows, and Choreo trajectory-following autonomous routines.

layers.name: Drive Subsystem
layers.description: Swerve drivetrain subsystem with four-module kinematics, gyro integration, odometry threading, and IO-layer abstractions for TalonFX hardware, simulation, and CTRE Pigeon 2 IMU.

layers.name: Shooter Subsystem
layers.description: Shooter coordinator with turret aiming, hood angle control, and dual-motor flywheel velocity management, including trajectory calculation utilities, shoot-on-the-move compensation, and IO-layer abstractions for hardware and simulation.

layers.name: Intake & Rollers Subsystem
layers.description: Game piece acquisition and indexing mechanisms including the intake pivot arm, intake rollers, spindexer, and kicker with IO-layer abstractions, jam detection, and LaserCAN sensor integration for fuel feeding.

layers.name: Peripheral Subsystems
layers.description: Climb, vision, and LED subsystems providing elevator-based climbing with TalonFX control, multi-camera AprilTag localization via Limelight, and addressable LED feedback for alliance colors and scoring indicators.

layers.name: Utility & Framework Support
layers.description: Shared utilities providing pose estimation, geometry conversions, alliance flipping, Phoenix 6 helpers, tunable number support, game piece physics simulation, match shift timing, and custom AdvantageKit logging infrastructure.

layers.name: Autonomous Trajectory Data
layers.description: Choreo choreography project and trajectory files defining swerve drive waypoints, velocity constraints, and multi-segment autonomous paths for scoring, feeding, climbing, and bump sequences, plus AprilTag field layouts for vision localization.

layers.name: Build System & Configuration
layers.description: GradleRIO build configuration, Gradle wrapper, WPILib vendor dependencies (Phoenix6, AdvantageKit, ChoreoLib, libgrapplefrc), simulation GUI settings, IDE preferences, CI pipeline, and project documentation.

layers.name: 3D Robot Models
layers.description: AdvantageScope 3D visualization assets including GLB robot models and articulation configs for the 2025 and 2026 competition robots, used for simulation dashboard rendering of turret, hood, and intake components.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: Main.java is the JVM entry point that bootstraps the FRC robot by calling RobotBase.startRobot with the Robot class constructor. It contains no other logic per WPILib convention -- all initialization is delegated to Robot.java, which extends LoggedRobot, initializes AdvantageKit logging, instantiates RobotContainer, and dispatches mode-specific lifecycle callbacks (autonomous, teleop, test, simulation).
tour.languageLesson: Java's method reference syntax (Robot::new) passes a constructor as a functional interface argument. WPILib uses this to instantiate your Robot class at the right point in its framework lifecycle, similar to how a dependency injection container works.

tour.title: Robot Configuration Hub
tour.description: RobotContainer is the central dependency injection hub with a fan-out of 49 -- by far the highest in the codebase. It instantiates every subsystem (drive, shooter, intake, climb, vision) with either real hardware IO or simulation IO implementations based on the current mode (Constants.currentMode), wires Xbox controller button bindings to commands, and configures fuel simulation for the 2026 game. Understanding this file gives you the complete map of what the robot can do.
tour.languageLesson: The IO-layer pattern used here is a form of the Strategy pattern: RobotContainer selects between hardware IO (e.g., ModuleIOTalonFX) and simulation IO (e.g., ModuleIOSim) implementations at construction time via a switch statement on the runtime mode. This lets the same subsystem code run on real hardware or in physics simulation without modification.

tour.title: Swerve Drive Subsystem
tour.description: The Drive subsystem is the robot's core mobility system, managing four swerve modules with independent steering and drive motors. Drive.java coordinates gyro integration, odometry updates via PoseManager, Choreo trajectory following for autonomous, and SysId characterization routines. Each swerve module is encapsulated by Module.java, which handles drive/turn motor IO, setpoint optimization with cosine scaling, and hardware disconnect alerts.

tour.title: Drive IO Layer Pattern
tour.description: The IO-layer pattern is the architectural backbone of every subsystem. Each mechanism defines an interface (ModuleIO, GyroIO) with AutoLog-annotated input fields and default control methods. Hardware implementations (ModuleIOTalonFX, GyroIOPigeon2) talk to real motors and sensors via CTRE Phoenix 6, while simulation implementations (ModuleIOSim) use WPILib physics models. PhoenixOdometryThread is a singleton daemon that samples odometry from Phoenix 6 devices at high frequency using CANivore blocking calls.
tour.languageLesson: Java interfaces with default methods (introduced in Java 8) let IO interfaces provide no-op defaults so that simulation stubs only need to override the methods they care about. The @AutoLog annotation from AdvantageKit generates boilerplate logging code at compile time via annotation processing, similar to Lombok's approach.

tour.title: Shooter Coordinator
tour.description: The Shooter class is the highest fan-out subsystem after RobotContainer (16 outgoing edges), orchestrating three tightly coupled sub-mechanisms: the turret for azimuth aiming, the hood for elevation angle, and the flywheels for launch velocity. It uses ShooterUtil to compute launching parameters based on distance-keyed interpolating tree maps and supports shoot-on-the-move (SOTM) via iterative time-of-flight convergence. The Shooter extends VirtualSubsystem so it runs its periodic() without needing WPILib Subsystem registration.

tour.title: Turret, Hood & Flywheels
tour.description: Building on the Shooter coordinator from Step 5, these are the three sub-mechanisms it controls. Turret.java features dual-encoder absolute position solving with multi-revolution angle wrapping and trapezoid motion profiling. Hood.java manages the launch angle with current-based zeroing. Flywheels.java runs a state machine (RUN/STOP/IDLE/VOLTS) with debounced at-goal detection for precise velocity control. Each follows the same IO-layer pattern seen in the drive subsystem.

tour.title: Intake & Roller Pipeline
tour.description: The intake system forms a game piece pipeline: the IntakePivot arm deploys to pick up fuel, IntakeRollers spin to grab it, the Spindexer indexes pieces into the shooter with stator-current-based jam detection and LED feedback, and the Kicker feeds them to the flywheels using LaserCAN-based launch counting. The 'jork' oscillation mode -- rapidly raising and lowering the intake -- is a novel mechanism for settling game pieces.

tour.title: Vision & Pose Estimation
tour.description: Vision.java processes AprilTag detections from four Limelight cameras, filtering invalid measurements based on tag count, field boundaries, rotation speed, and distance before feeding validated pose estimates to PoseManager. PoseManager is the third most depended-upon file (fan-in of 9), wrapping WPILib's SwerveDrivePoseEstimator to fuse odometry and vision data, track robot velocity, and manage game piece positions with nearest-neighbor queries.

tour.title: Command Factories
tour.description: WPILib's command-based framework composes robot actions as Command objects. DriveCommands produces joystick drive modes (field-relative, angle-locked, auto-aim toward the hub, snake drive) and characterization routines. RobotCommands provides reusable composite commands for shooting, intaking, stowing, jorking, unjamming, and system tests. These factories are consumed by both RobotContainer (for teleop button bindings) and Autos (for autonomous sequences).

tour.title: Autonomous Routines
tour.description: Autos.java defines all autonomous routines using Choreo trajectory following, including multi-segment scoring, feeding, climbing, and bump sequences. Each routine is composed by chaining RobotCommands helpers with trajectory-following commands from the Drive subsystem. The LoggedAutoChooser lazily loads routines on selection via NetworkTables, and the Choreo project file (Autos.chor) defines the swerve drive robot configuration and 12 named field waypoints used across all trajectory files.

tour.title: Shared Utilities
tour.description: The utility layer contains the most depended-upon files in the codebase. LoggedTunableNumber (fan-in of 17, the highest) enables runtime parameter hot-swapping via NetworkTables during development. FieldConstants defines all field geometry (hub, bumps, trenches, tower positions) and loads AprilTag layouts. AllianceFlipUtil mirrors coordinates for red alliance. GeomUtil converts between WPILib geometry types. These utilities are consumed across nearly every subsystem and command.

tour.title: Peripheral Subsystems
tour.description: The Climb subsystem uses an elevator mechanism with voltage-based up/down commands and position feedback for extending and retracting. The Leds subsystem is a singleton VirtualSubsystem managing a 150-LED addressable strip, displaying team colors, alliance-aware patterns, e-stop breathing, and scoring/jamming indicators. FuelSim is a comprehensive 3D physics simulation for game pieces on the field, handling gravity, collisions, intake detection, and hub scoring.

tour.title: Build System & Dependencies
tour.description: The GradleRIO build system targets a RoboRIO ARM processor with Java 17. build.gradle defines deployment configuration (JVM tuning, static file deploy), WPILib and AdvantageKit dependencies, Lombok annotation processing, JUnit 5 testing, and Spotless code formatting. The vendordeps directory contains WPILib vendor dependency descriptors for Phoenix 6 (CTRE motor controllers), AdvantageKit (logging), ChoreoLib (trajectory planning), and libgrapplefrc (LaserCAN sensors).

tour.title: CI Pipeline & Field Data
tour.description: The GitHub Actions CI workflow builds the FRC robot code on every push and pull request using the WPILib RoboRIO cross-compilation container and Gradle, ensuring the code always compiles for the target ARM platform. The AprilTag field layout JSON files define 3D poses for all competition fiducial markers across both AndyMark and welded field variants, which the Vision subsystem (Step 8) loads to enable on-field localization.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use YAML with 'on' triggers for events, 'jobs' for parallel work units, and 'steps' for sequential execution within a job. Using a specialized container image (wpilib/roborio-cross-ubuntu) ensures the build environment matches the target RoboRIO processor architecture.
